title: fix(pm): a size refusal is a refusal — post-stamped stops reporting a real 422 as a missing route
body:
Fixes #18843

Clause-②: no

`post-stamped.mjs` reported a real HTTP 422 from the platform as exit 3
`EXIT_PREREQUISITE_NOT_MET` — 「no route, no act at all」 — and prescribed a
transport remedy. This gives the size refusal an exit class of its own, whose
text carries the bytes SENT, the measured cap for THAT surface, and the remedy
that works; and it homes the comment cap beside `ISSUE_BODY_LIMIT`, which the
card says is the same card.

## The fixture, verbatim, and where it came from

Built from the record on probe objectstack#18826 — comment id **5722505167**,
written 2026-09-17T23:19:18Z. ⛔ No new oversized write was made anywhere to
reproduce this. Captured there from `POST /issues/{n}/comments` at 262,145 bytes:

```json
{"resource":"IssueComment","code":"unprocessable","field":"data",
 "message":"Body is too long (maximum is 65536 characters)"}
```

## The two readings the dispatch carried as unmeasured, now measured

1. **The 422 message is NOT the same string on the two endpoints.** The record
   is explicit: the create side answers `Body is too long (maximum is 65536
   characters)`, and `PATCH /issues/comments/{id}` answers the same sentence with
   a lower-case `body`; `POST /issues` says it twice. So the trigger is
   case-insensitive rather than an equality — an equality pinned to the
   create-side capital would have left the update side at exit 3. Pinned in both
   spellings, and the ablation below proves the flag is load-bearing.
   ⚠️ One correction to the dispatch's framing: `PATCH /issues/comments/{id}` is
   not a surface this tool ever writes. Its two write surfaces are
   `POST /issues/{n}/comments` (`--comment`) and `PATCH /issues/{n}` (`--body`).
   Both caps are declared; the update-side spelling still matters, because it is
   the second measured spelling of the sentence the trigger keys on.
2. **The two caps live as two constants, beside each other in
   `check-half-states.mjs`.** `COMMENT_BODY_LIMIT` is declared after
   `MARKDOWN_BODY_BUDGET`, with its own bisection provenance. It is homed there
   rather than in `post-stamped.mjs` on a measured ground: five workflow comments
   (`cross-repo-issue-closer.yml`, `merge-queue-triage.yml`,
   `scheduled-full-run-card.yml`, `test-nightly-tiers.yml`) already send a reader
   to `ISSUE_BODY_LIMIT` in that file for the number and warn against
   re-deriving 65,536 — the folklore grows back wherever one of two caps is kept
   somewhere else. ⛔ Two constants and not one shared number: two surfaces
   measured independently that agree is not one measurement, and the day the
   platform moves one a shared number would lie about the other.

## The exit register, before and after

| code | before | after |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | written, and everything sent is on the platform | unchanged |
| 1 | usage | unchanged |
| 2 | the body broke the stamp contract | unchanged |
| 3 | PREREQUISITE NOT MET — no route, no token, no act at all | unchanged, and it now prints what the platform said |
| 4 | written, and the platform did NOT store it | unchanged |
| 5 | — | **TOO LARGE — the platform ANSWERED and refused the body for its size. Nothing written; shorten or split it. ⛔ Not a route problem.** |

`EXIT_TOO_LARGE = 5` is declared in `post-stamped.mjs` beside `EXIT_NOT_STORED`.
The usage text, the not-stored text and the prerequisite text each name it, so a
reader of a 3 or a 4 learns the fifth code exists.

## The reader test

A seat that sends a 300 KB comment body now reads: **exit 5, 307,200 byte(s)
sent, cap 262,144 bytes for a comment, 45,056 byte(s) over it, shorten or split
the body** — and ⛔ not a word about routes or tokens. Verbatim from the
`--self-test` fixture:

```text
post-stamped: TOO LARGE — the platform ANSWERED this write and REFUSED it: the body is over the cap
for this surface. NOTHING WAS WRITTEN.

  Sent to objectstack-ai/objectstack#18843: 307,200 byte(s) as a comment (`POST /issues/{n}/comments`).
  The measured cap for a comment is 262,144 bytes — UTF-8 BYTES, bisected on
  objectstack#18826, one byte either side.
  This body is 45,056 byte(s) over it.

  The platform said: Validation Failed · Body is too long (maximum is 65536 characters)
  ⛔ Its number is FALSE in unit and value — the same fleet measured a 262,144-BYTE comment stored,
     four times what that sentence claims as a maximum.
```

## What the class deliberately does NOT take

- **Not every 422.** The issues listing refuses deep pagination — page 99 stores,
  page 100 answers 422 (measured 2026-08-31, recorded in
  `check-half-states.mjs`) — and that refusal is about a cursor. It keeps its 3,
  pinned as a control, as do the same sentence on a 403, a 500 and a 200.
- **Not the platform's number.** The trigger stops before `maximum is`, so
  keying on a false clause cannot un-classify the refusal the day GitHub
  corrects its own text; a text carrying only that clause is pinned NOT to
  classify.
- **Not the read path.** A read sends no body, so the `--body` pre-read keeps its
  PREREQUISITE reading unchanged.
- **Not a widened `--body` story.** Over the cap, `PATCH /issues/{n}` refuses
  SILENTLY (200, old body kept, #18793), which is exit 4's population; only a
  422 the platform actually answers reaches 5.

## A refusal the cap does not explain

If the platform ever refuses a body at or under the measured cap, the text says
the refusal CONTRADICTS the reading and asks for a re-measurement rather than
printing an overage of zero — `over` is `null`, never 0. The ordinary over-cap
text is pinned NOT to carry that sentence.

## Self-test counts

| battery ledger | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `post-stamped --self-test` cases | 349 | **402** |
| `post-stamped` batteries (floor) | 13 | **14** |
| new battery `the size refusal: …` (registered/floor) | — | **53 / 53** |
| `check-half-states --self-test` cases | 4,963 | **4,978** |
| battery `ISSUE_BODY_LIMIT measured cap` (registered/floor) | 40 / 37 | **55 / 52** |

The check-half-states "before" is the merge base `d5ccfb4e3`: 4,978 minus the 15
cases this PR registers. Two independent readings agree on it — the dispatch
recorded 4,963 at PR #18911's head, and this branch measures 4,921 at its own
branch point `625db0e85`, which is before #18911 landed. Both floors RISE by
exactly the number of cases added; neither is held flat.

## Ablations — each mutation proven on disk, each restore proven against HEAD

All four through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which asserts the anchor count
fell, the blob hash changed, and after restore that the blob equals HEAD's and
`git diff HEAD` is empty.

| mutation | expected | observed |
|---|---|---|
| drop the `i` flag from `BODY_TOO_LONG_RE` | red | **19 of 402 cases fail by name**; the lower-case pin stays green, so the ablation discriminates |
| put `ROUTE_REMEDY` in the size text's `Fix:` line | red | **exactly the 2 held-apart pins fail** |
| `COMMENT_BODY_LIMIT` 262144 → 65536 | red | **5 of 4,978 cases fail by name** |
| delete `UTF-8 BYTES` from the comment cap's docblock | red | **exactly 1 pin fails** — and the sibling docblock also contains that phrase, so a mis-pointed extractor would have stayed green |

⭐ **The first ablation found a defect in this PR's own first draft.** It came
back GREEN: the classifier was rebuilding the regex from `.source` with the
flags retyped at the call site, so the exported constant documented a rule it
did not carry and every case-insensitivity pin was vacuous. Fixed in
`36ba41a64`, after which the same ablation turns 19 cases red. A second pass
(`290acfad0`) made those pins fail by NAME rather than crash on a TypeError
before the verdict machinery ran.

## Gates

Derived in the worktree with
`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`
at HEAD `0e5e054d3`: **39 families, all 39 run, all exit 0**, exit codes captured
by redirect-then-`$?`. `--ran` reconciliation: 39 derived, 39 run, 0 UNRUN. The
first derivation (before the merge, one path) gave 29; adding
`check-half-states.mjs` grew it by 10 and those were run too. Each edited
script's own `--self-test` is in that set
(`check:pm-post-stamped`, `check:pm-half-states`). `git grep` of both filenames
under tests finds no separate suite — the `--self-test` IS the suite.

**ESLint was not narrowed at all.** The repo-wide run is the one that was taken:
`pnpm lint` (= `eslint . --no-inline-config`, this repo's only style authority)
**exit 0** at HEAD `0e5e054d3`. The targeted run over the two changed files is
there too — 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings — but it is not what this PR rests on.

## Acceptance notes

- **Exit 3 still hosts other refusals the platform ANSWERED.** The deep
  pagination 422 is the measured one, and its remedy text is a route remedy just
  as wrongly. ⛔ Not filed: it is unreachable through this tool (a comment list
  would need 10,000 comments to reach page 100), so it is an observation, not a
  reproducible defect.
- **`rest()` now surfaces the platform's sentence on every non-2xx**, which is
  the same defect family (the tool discarding the answer it was given) and is
  mechanically part of this change; it is not a separate fix.
